speaker: Unknown
en: We're really at an inflection point because you have the birth of essentially coin-operated intelligence at scale.
zh: 我们真的处于一个转折点，因为你看到了本质上大规模投币式智能的诞生。

speaker: Unknown
en: The internet is really kind of stagnated a bit from protocol design.
zh: 互联网在协议设计方面确实有点停滞了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like not a lot of new stuff.
zh: 没有太多新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of it's built on top.
zh: 一切都是在其之上构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Erasing that is kind of what I'm trying to go for.
zh: 抹掉这些就是我想要达到的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're saying is you've actually built this transient way for folks to connect and chat without there being any record.
zh: 你所说的是，你实际上构建了一种临时性的方式，让人们在没有留下任何记录的情况下连接和聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: The really big problem is on WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, Telegram.
zh: 真正的大问题在于 WhatsApp、Signal、iMessage、Telegram 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of those applications disguise themselves as you sending something to somebody else.
zh: 所有这些应用都把自己伪装成你在给另一个人发送信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're really sending something to a server.
zh: 但你实际上是把信息发送给一台服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is like, okay, well, whose servers are those?
zh: 问题是，好吧，那些是谁的服务器？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's coming at such an important inflection point for like the future of our country, tech, and to just have this conversation that seems to be manipulated to some end.
zh: 这正处在我们国家的未来、技术的未来如此重要的一个转折点上，而这场对话似乎被操纵以达到某种目的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels very manipulated.
zh: 感觉非常被操纵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to me, the future of our tech is needing to build this infrastructure now if we're crippling it.
zh: 对我来说，我们技术的未来需要现在就构建这种基础设施，否则我们就是在削弱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The internet was designed to connect people directly.
zh: 互联网的设计初衷是让人与人直接连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, much of what we do online passes through someone else's server, along with an enormous amount of data about us.
zh: 今天，我们在网上做的许多事情都要经过别人的服务器，还有大量关于我们的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, A16Z's Joel De La Garza sits down with internet infrastructure pioneer Barrett Lyon to talk about DocsNet, his attempt to rethink that architecture from the ground up.
zh: 在本期节目中，A16Z 的 Joel De La Garza 与互联网基础设施先驱 Barrett Lyon 坐下来，谈谈 DocsNet——他试图从根本上重新思考这一架构的尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Barrett explains why VPNs aren't enough, how DocsNet enables encrypted peer-to-peer communication without a central server sitting in the middle, and why the company owns its infrastructure all the way down to the hardware.
zh: Barrett 解释了为什么 VPN 不够，DocsNet 如何在没有中央服务器居中的情况下实现加密的点对点通信，以及为什么这家公司的自有基础设施一直深入到硬件层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also discuss what happens when decades of online tracking meet cheap AI, why Barrett thinks internet protocol development has stagnated, and what it would take to bring back some of the openness and experimentation of the early internet.
zh: 他们还讨论了当数十年的在线追踪遇上廉价的 AI 会发生什么，为什么 Barrett 认为互联网协议的开发已经停滞，以及需要什么才能找回早期互联网的某种开放性和实验精神。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, today we're joined by Barrett Lyon, perhaps one of the most interesting people in tech.
zh: 好的，今天我们请来了 Barrett Lyon，可能是科技界最有意思的人物之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a lot of stories to share, and I am always kind of blown away every time we catch up because you tell me a new story that just puts everything I've ever done in ailing comparison.
zh: 我有很多故事可以分享，而我们每次见面时我总是有点被震撼，因为你会告诉我一个新故事，把我做过的一切都比得相形见绌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the most interesting one I heard recently, and I had never heard it before, and this was during a period, I believe, where we were investors in your previous company.
zh: 我觉得我最近听到的最有意思的一个故事，而且我以前从未听说过，那是在一个时期——我相信当时我们还是你上一家公司的投资人——

speaker: Unknown
en: was you are a pilot, you have a pilot's license, and you decided to optimize your life by flying places, and you had an unfortunate experience, I believe, flying back from one of our meetings.
zh: 就是你是一名飞行员，你有飞行执照，你决定通过飞行来优化你的生活，而且我相信你有一次不幸的经历，是从我们其中一次会议飞回来的途中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, I mean, one day I was driving to work in the Bay Area, and I realized it was almost 45 minutes, which used to be 15, and my family lives up in the Tahoe region, so I'm like, well...
zh: 是的，嗯，有一天我开车去湾区上班，我意识到差不多要 45 分钟，而以前只要 15 分钟，我家人住在 Tahoe 地区，所以我就想，嗯……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the plane can fly there at about the same time.
zh: 我觉得飞机飞过去大概需要差不多的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I could just commute that way.
zh: 也许我可以就那样通勤。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was before work from home was like codified by COVID.
zh: 那是在远程办公被 COVID 确立下来之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had like a need to physically be present.
zh: 所以我需要亲自到场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I started flying and...
zh: 所以是的，我开始飞了，然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: So your daily driver was a daily flyer?
zh: 所以你的日常座驾成了日常座机？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I put 1,300 hours on a Cirrus.
zh: 我在一架 Cirrus 上飞了 1,300 个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, one day after meeting here, I left and got in the plane, took off from San Carlos, and somewhere over Oakland Airport, engines started acting up.
zh: 然后，有一天在这里开完会，我离开后上了飞机，从 San Carlos 起飞，在 Oakland 机场上空的某个地方，发动机开始出问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought maybe it was like some sort of water in the fuel or something, but I climbed up, cleared Bravo, and felt like I was okay.
zh: 我以为可能是燃料里进了水之类的，但我爬升，飞出了 Bravo 空域，觉得自己应该没事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then right after that thought, I lost pretty much all power.
zh: 然后就在那个念头之后，我几乎失去了全部动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what went through your head immediately after that?
zh: 在那之后你脑子里立刻想到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, I messaged my friends and said, hey guys, I have an emergency.
zh: 实际上，我给我的朋友们发了消息说，嘿，各位，我遇到紧急情况了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love you.
zh: 爱你们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, I just declared emergency and just tried to think, okay, where do I crash and not hurt people?
zh: 我不知道，我就是宣布了紧急状态，然后试着想，好吧，我在哪里坠机才不会伤到人？

speaker: Unknown
en: I found a field and then it turns out...
zh: 我找到了一块田地，然后结果是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I was up pretty high, and there was a giant airport right next to us.
zh: 我当时飞得挺高，旁边就有一个巨大的机场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not Oakland, but it was Buchanan Field.
zh: 不是 Oakland，而是 Buchanan Field。

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget the name of the town.
zh: 我忘了那个镇的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a giant old military airport.
zh: 那是一个巨大的老军用机场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, in Alameda.
zh: 哦，在 Alameda。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it was the other one on the other side of the mountain range there.
zh: 不，是山脉另一边的另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Buchanan Field is the name of it, I believe.
zh: 我相信它的名字叫 Buchanan Field。

speaker: Unknown
en: But anyway, I landed there.
zh: 不过总之，我降落在那里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before that, I kind of went to this field and I was like, all right, well, I've got a parachute, ballistics parachute.
zh: 但在那之前，我有点进入了这个状态，我当时想，好吧，我有一个降落伞，弹道降落伞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I pull it?
zh: 我要拉吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was thinking, all right, well, when I read all these crash reports, the reason the pilot dies is because they didn't use the parachute.
zh: 我当时在想，好吧，我读过所有这些坠机报告，飞行员死掉的原因就是他们没用降落伞。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, well, the airport's right there and I'm still in the air flying.
zh: 我心想，嗯，机场就在那儿，而我还在空中飞着。

speaker: Unknown
en: And isn't that a funny quirk of that plane, that it's technically the safest plane ever made, but yet it's involved in the most crashes because people never use the safety feature?
zh: 这架飞机是不是有个很好笑的怪癖，它在技术上是史上最安全的飞机，但它却卷入了最多的坠机事故，因为人们从来不用那个安全功能？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and I mean, it does work, but it destroys the plane, too.
zh: 嗯，我的意思是，它确实有用，但它也会毁掉飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it shoots a rock out of the back of the tail and rips all this stuff out and ruins the plane.
zh: 它会从机尾后面射出一个东西出来，把一堆东西扯烂，把飞机毁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's not a guarantee that you're going to land nicely on the ground.
zh: 而且也不能保证你会漂亮地降落到地面上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, the seats, I think, are made with a crumple and packed thing.
zh: 事实上，我想那些座椅是做成那种压溃吸能的结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you do hit the ground, it absorbs compression.
zh: 所以当你撞到地面时，它能吸收压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is all playing out over how long a period of time?
zh: 这一切是在多长的时间内发生的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I don't know.
zh: 哦，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably like minutes or less.
zh: 大概几分钟或更短吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe less.
zh: 也许更短。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then anyway, I just made the call to land and landed, rolled right onto the transient parking spot.
zh: 然后不管怎样，我做了降落的决定，降落了，直接滑进了过境停机位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was calm.
zh: 我很平静。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was kind of frustrated and a little confused when I got out of the plane.
zh: 我下飞机的时候有点沮丧，还有点茫然。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, those big firetruck things, the huge ones that look like some kid made them, but they're big.
zh: 然后，你知道那些大型消防车，那种巨大的、看起来像某个小孩做出来的那种，但它们很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: The guy gets out of that, shakes my hand.
zh: 那家伙从车里出来，和我握手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then that's when the fear hit me because I'm like, that's the guy scraping my brains off the
zh: 然后就在那时恐惧袭上心头，因为我想，这就是那个要把我脑子从……刮下来的家伙

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, oh no, this is the guy that puts the fire out.
zh: 我心想，哦不，这是那个灭火的家伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was close.
zh: 刚才真是好险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I'm like, now what do I do?
zh: 然后我就想，现在我该怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to get home somehow, rent a car, drive home.
zh: 我得想办法回家，租辆车，开回家。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was kind of the end of it for me.
zh: 对我来说，这基本就是终点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, the risk is too high.
zh: 我当时想，风险太高了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kept the plane for a while and ended up ferrying it out to Las Vegas and selling it.
zh: 我把飞机保留了一段时间，最后把它飞渡到拉斯维加斯卖掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you ever find out what the issue or the cause was?
zh: 你后来有查出问题或原因是什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was like three really weird things at the same time.
zh: 有，好像是三件很奇怪的事情同时发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was a piece of metal on the air intake control valve, or the kind of a lever broke off and sucked into the air intake manifold.
zh: 一个是进气控制阀上的一块金属，或者说是那种操纵杆断掉了，被吸进了进气歧管。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it went down to the oil pan and it was crushed into cylinder three and six, I think.
zh: 然后它掉到了油底壳里，我记得它被压进了三号和六号气缸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then that caused an electrical problem with something with the spark, which was controlled by a brand new electronic ignition system.
zh: 然后这导致了一个电气问题，和点火有关的东西出了问题，那是由一套全新的电子点火系统控制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That stopped working.
zh: 那个停止工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then I lost half ignition.
zh: 所以我就失去了一半的点火。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at the same time, my magneto on the other side, which is the backup, also stopped working.
zh: 然后与此同时，另一边的我的磁电机，也就是备用系统，也停止工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was like three, it was like a cascading, strange failure.
zh: 所以这就像是三个……像是一个连锁的、奇怪的故障。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it was also weird too, because on the ground, the magneto was kind of working a little bit.
zh: 而且还有一点也很奇怪，因为在地面上，磁电机还有点能工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it would start, but then when you went to higher RPMs, it just went bye-bye.
zh: 所以它能启动，但当你把转速拉高时，它就直接拜拜了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, yeah.
zh: 总之，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's what it was.
zh: 情况就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took a while to figure it out.
zh: 花了一段时间才查明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that was an interesting drive home.
zh: 是啊，那是一段挺有意思的回家路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Happens.
zh: 这种事会发生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you understand why the pope kisses the ground when he gets off the plane, right?
zh: 现在你明白为什么教皇下飞机时要亲吻地面了吧，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's ever another plane in my life, it will have less moving parts.
zh: 如果我人生中还有下一次坐飞机的机会，那架飞机的活动部件会更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully a backup, backup pilots and redundancy.
zh: 希望有备份、备用飞行员和冗余。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you fly a lot, you kind of, you're increasing your, I guess your risk level a little bit.
zh: 而且如果你经常坐飞机，你多少会……我想你的风险水平会稍微增加一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that sort of probably triggered a lot of things.
zh: 那可能触发了很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know we're here to talk about your new venture, which sort of is something very, I'd say very different for you.
zh: 我知道我们今天是来聊你的新项目的，这对你来说，我想说，是非常不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems more like a more close to home, more important.
zh: 它看起来更贴近内心，更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe we can talk a bit about Docs.
zh: 那么也许我们可以聊一聊 Docs。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: And why you decided to build, well, first of all, what is it?
zh: 以及你为什么决定开发它，首先，它是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What caused you to do it?
zh: 是什么促使你做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of maybe you're thinking around why this is important.
zh: 还有你为什么认为这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why now?
zh: 为什么是现在？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, okay, so DocsNet, first of all, maybe I should explain the name.
zh: 好吧，那么 DocsNet，首先，也许我应该解释一下这个名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a kid, my hacker name was Docs.
zh: 小时候，我的黑客名字就是 Docs。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I started a business in high school with my high school friend called DocsNet.
zh: 然后我在高中和一个高中朋友创办了一家公司，叫 DocsNet。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was before cloud, and we were renting server, basically giving user accounts for money.
zh: 那是在云之前，我们租用服务器，基本上是以收费的方式提供用户账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally legit business in high school, we were making pretty good money.
zh: 高中里完全合法的生意，我们赚了不少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Were these shell accounts?
zh: 那些是 shell 账户吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, shell accounts.
zh: 对，shell 账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we were selling shell accounts for $5 a month, but we had 1,000 users.
zh: 我们以每月 5 美元的价格卖 shell 账户，有 1,000 个用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had all these features and people liked it.
zh: 我们有很多功能，大家都很喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was actually a little community around it for a while.
zh: 而且确实一度围绕它形成了一个小社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got out of high school and shut it all down and started my career.
zh: 高中毕业后，我把它全部关掉，开始了我的职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I kept a domain.
zh: 但我保留了一个域名。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also I'm very fascinated about protocol design and the fact that the internet has really kind of stagnated a bit from protocol design.
zh: 而且我对协议设计非常着迷，互联网在协议设计方面其实已经有点停滞了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like not a lot of new stuff.
zh: 几乎没有什么新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of it's built on top.
zh: 一切都是在其之上构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's that.
zh: 所以这是其一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just noticing the shift of censorship and people's privacy being eroded and all of this kind of thing kind of
zh: 然后是注意到审查的转变、人们的隐私被侵蚀，以及这一类事情

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the uprise of VPN made it really interesting to make kind of an alternative network that kind of is designed from the ground up to protect people from advertisers, trackers, malware, and foreign adversaries trying to learn about what you're doing.
zh: 然后 VPN 的兴起让构建一种替代网络变得非常有趣，这种网络从底层设计就旨在保护人们免受广告商、追踪器、恶意软件以及试图了解你行踪的外国对手的侵害。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I mean, the original promise of the internet was this incredible marketplace of ideas, unrestricted, no censorship, right?
zh: 嗯，我是说，互联网最初的承诺是这样一个不可思议的思想市场，不受限制、没有审查，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of original...
zh: 我想很多最初……

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the original people around the founding of what became the internet were free speech maximalists.
zh: 很多在后来成为互联网的这个东西创立之初的原始参与者，都是言论自由的极致主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was sort of a very specific crowd, and I think over the last couple of years that, to your point, has shifted pretty incredibly, right?
zh: 那是一个很特定的群体，我想在过去几年里，正如你所说，这已经发生了相当惊人的转变，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and it's in the hands of a few.
zh: 是的，而且它掌握在少数人手中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, for example, China's a good example.
zh: 比如说，中国就是一个很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was ChinaNetCom, ChinaTelecom, and those, or is it ChinaNetCom?
zh: 那时候是 ChinaNetCom、ChinaTelecom，或者说，是 ChinaNetCom 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, either way, it's a pretty good chokehold of the entire population using that network as an opportunity to force people into different decision-making processes.
zh: 总之，不管是哪一个，它对整个使用该网络的民众形成了相当牢固的扼制，把网络当作迫使人们进入不同决策过程的机会。
